mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate at or below 0.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as investors seek yield in equities.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase above 8.0% signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending confidence, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when UNRATE > 8.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strengthening consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through revenue growth expectations.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive returns in >50% of cases (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 95.0 in 3 months indicates manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate output and earnings expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in retail sales (RSAFS) reflects strong consumer spending that supports corporate revenue growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when RSAFS is rising (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase above 2.25 signals accelerating inflation, prompting Federal Reserve rate hike expectations that reduce equity attractiveness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.25 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment (PAYEMS) and increases in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate labor market contraction, reducing consumer income and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of falling PAYEMS and rising UNRATE fails to produce negative returns in >50% of cases (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 8.0% and rising in 3 months) reflects persistent labor market weakness that suppresses consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
regime_hint: high unemployment and labor market deterioration
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when UNRATE > 8.0% and rising (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
